doc.title: Howard Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019

title: Favorite recordings and Miles Davis in Montreux
summary: He likes all four of his own records; Miles never listened back, and the Montreux concert with Gil Evans's arrangements.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Do you have favorite recordings of your own?
I like all of my recordings. There are only four of them, or is there five? Four.
I’m happy to hear you say that because some people say, “Oh, I never listen to what I record. I could have done better.”
Yeah. Well Miles Davis always said that but not for any reason like that.

He said that once it’s recorded he doesn’t want to hear it anymore because that’s going back. He doesn’t want to go back. He only wants to go forward. As a result, when we did, the last thing he did with the orchestra in Montreux with the Gil Evans arrangements and Quincy Jones conducting, when he was doing that, Gil Goldstein had sent him the parts in March or something like that, for this concert in the summer. He hadn’t cracked those parts open and he wasn’t ready with the chops or the concept when the concert actually went on. He got away with it. He only got lost once and he had Wallace Roney to pick up for him.
